Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular Meeting of the Cabot City Council at 7:10
pm, following the Work Session. Council Member James Reid led the prayer, and Council
Member Ed Long led the pledge of allegiance.

Roll Calf

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present: Brandon
Hillenburg, James Reid, Maggie Cope, Ed Long, Kyle Pickard, Matt Webber, and
Corey Spangler. Stephen Redd was absent. Others present were Mayor Kincade,
City Attorney Ben Hooper, Deputy City Attorney Courtnie Holt, and City
Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

Mr. Reid, seconded by Mr. Hillenburg, motioned to approve the minutes of the
September 22 meeting. The motion passed unanimously.

Mr. Reid, seconded by Mr. Hillenburg, moved only to read the legislation by title.
The motion passed unanimously.

Cit mncil

OLD BUSINESS: AMENDED ORDINANCE NO. 26 OF 2025 — AN ORDINANCE TO
AMEND THE CODE OF CABOT SECTION 2-208; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES was
read by title only by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Mr. Hillenburg
motioned to adopt, seconded by Mr. Pickard. Motion passed by a vote of 6-1. Mr.
Spangler voted no.

PUBLIC HEARING

Mayor Kincade recessed the regular council meeting at 7:14 pm and convened a
Public Hearing at the same time. He stated that the purpose of the hearing was
to receive public comment regarding the fixing of rates, fees, and deposits for
wastewater and other water services provided by Cabot Waterworks. Mayor
Kincade announced that he had received a text message asking whether Cabot
Waterworks could address the buildup on appliances resulting from water use.
No individuals appeared to speak either in favor of or in opposition to the matter.
The Public Hearing was closed at 7:16 pm, and Mayor Kincade reconvened the
regular council meeting at 7:16 pm.

WHEREAS, due to violations of the City of Cabot’s Code of Ordinances, the City has
expended funds for services rendered and/or performed by and/or on behalf of the City of Cabot
for certain work on real properties located within the city limits to remove/modify noncompliant
conditions. A list of the relevant real properties is attached hereto as Exhibit A.

WHEREAS, despite notice and demand, the property owners at issue have not paid the
amounts due to the City for services rendered and/or performed as detailed herein; and

WHEREAS, pursuant to Arkansas law, tax liens may be created and certified for these
real properties and record property owners as listed in Exhibit A. Furthermore, the lien amounts
should be certified for inclusion in the annual real estate tax statements prepared by the Lonoke
County Treasurer’s Office or other appropriate county office.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: In accordance with the authority granted under A.C.A. 14-54-901 et seq.,
the Cabot City Council hereby authorizes the Mayor and/or the City Clerk~Treasurer to certify the
list of real properties and amounts due, plus ten percent, attached hereto to the Lonoke County
Circuit Clerk’s Office, Lonoke County Treasurer’s Office, and any other appropriate office for
inclusion as tax liens on the annual real property tax statements for 2025. A list of the relevant
real properties is attached as Exhibit A and is hereby incorporated into this ordinance by this
reference. The real property and corresponding lien amounts listed therein are deemed confirmed

for the purposes of A.C.A. 14-54-903 and other relevant law.

RESOLUTION NO. 29 OF 2025

A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND CITY CLERK-
TREASURER TO ENTER INTO A CONTRACT WITH WASTE
CONNECTIONS FOR WASTE COLLECTION, RECYCLING, AND
RELATED SERVICES; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the City of Cabot is in need of waste collection, recycling, and related
services for 2026 and subsequent years; and

WHEREAS, the City followed the relevant provisions of state and local law in
submitting the matter for competitive bidding; and

WHEREAS, at the completion of the competitive bidding process the bids were opened
and read in the presence of the Mayor or his authorized representative as required by law, and
Waste Connections returned the lowest bid. A different service provider returned a nominally
lower bid, however that bid was a conditional bid. Conditional bids were specifically
disallowed under the bid documents provided to the bidders, and, as such, that service
provider’s bid was rejected, leaving Waste Connections as the lowest responsible bidder; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council hereby affirms that Waste Connections returned
the lowest responsible bid for waste collection, recycling, and related services, and that the
Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are therefore herein authorized to enter into an agreement with
Waste Connections for said services.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized to enter into
an agreement with Waste Connections for waste collection, recycling, and related services. The
agreement authorized herein is to be for an amount corresponding with Waste Connections’ bid
for these services and is to be otherwise broadly consistent with the attached Exhibit A,
incorporated herein by this reference. The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are further
authorized to execute any documents or take any other-actions needed to effectuate the
agreement authorized herein. The City Council acknowledges that the contract set forth in
Exhibit A may change before final execution as a result of the contract negotiation process.

SECTION 2: This resolution shall be in full force and effect from and after its passage.

Letter of Introduction

Waste Connections — Proposal for Waste Material Collection Services City of Cabot, Arkansas
Mayor Ken Kincade and Members of the Cabot City Council,

Waste Connections is pleased to submit this proposal for the collection of residential solid waste,
recyclables, and municipal facility waste for the City of Cabot. We are no stranger to your community—we
proudly served Cabot residents from approximately 2010 to 2020, delivering reliable, high-quality service
and building strong relationships with your city staff, council members, and residents. During that time,
our record was one of fair pricing, operational excellence, and exceptional customer service.

While circumstances beyond our control led to the contract’s award to another provider, we are aware of
concerns from residents and city leaders regarding the current level of service and communications. Many
in Cabot, including city employees and councilmembers, still remember Waste Connections as a
dependable, responsive partner—and we are eager for the opportunity to restore that trust, reliability, and
quality of service.

Locally, we provide residential, commercial, and recycling services to the City of Mountain Home, Austin,
Ash Flat, Horseshoe Bend, Cherokee Village, Salesville, Bull Shoals, Cotter, Calico Rock, Mammoth Spring,
and along with many others in Arkansas. Our established relationships and operational infrastructure with
over 50+ trucks and 115+ employees in the region will ensure a seamless and efficient transition for Cabot]

About Waste Connections

Waste Connections is one of the largest integrated solid waste services companies in North America,
serving more than nine million customers across 46 states. Our success is built on a local operating model—
each community we serve is supported by managers, drivers, and customer service staff who live and work
in the region. We believe in serving our communities, not just servicing contracts.

Our commitment to Cabot includes:

© Local Service, National Strength — The City will be serviced out of our Beebe Transfer Station (15.7 miles
from Cabot), ensuring proximity and responsiveness while drawing on our regional and national resources.

real properties and record property owners as listed in Exhibit A. Furthermore, the lien amounts
should be certified for inclusion in the annual real estate tax statements prepared by the Lonoke
County Treasurer’s Office or other appropriate county office.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

Circuit Clerk’s Office, Lonoke County Treasurer’s Office, and any other appropriate office for
inclusion as tax liens on the annual real property tax statements for 2025. A list of the relevant
real properties is attached as Exhibit A and is hereby incorporated into this ordinance by this

5.4.6 Platted Building Lines and Buffers — Current Code

a. Building lines for residential lots shall be at least twenty-five (25) feet from each street
property line except in the following circumstances:

i. Residential lots fronting on a minor arterial street shall have a platted building line
not less than thirty-five (35) feet from the right-of-way line;

ii. Residential lots fronting on principal arterials shall have a platted building line not
less than forty (40) feet from the right-of-way line.

b. Along arterial streets where it is desirable to limit curb access, building lines shall be
established on both frontages of double frontage lots. Along the line of lots abutting such
traffic artery, a restricted access easement of at least ten (10) feet, across which there
shall be no right-of-vehicle access permitted, shall be provided.

c. Multi-family (more than two units attached) subdivisions abutting single-family
subdivisions or areas zoned for single-family use shall protect such areas from potential
nuisance by providing a minimum forty (40)-foot buffer strip and a six (6)-foot fence of
wood or masonry, extending along the entire abutting portion of the property. In those
instances where drives or parking areas are proposed for intrusion into the buffer strip, a
minimum of fifteen (15) feet shall be retained in its natural state. If ground cover and
trees are sparse or have been removed, the fifteen (15)-foot strip shall be replanted with
cover of the type natural to the area. No building, outside storage areas or sanitation
equipment shall be permitted within the fifteen (15)-foot area.

d. In those instances where a twenty-five (25)-foot permanent landscaped rear yard is
provided, the buffer may be reduced to twenty-five (25) feet. In this arrangement, no
structural or physical improvements are allowed within the twenty-five (25)-foot buffer.
The six (6)-foot fence required will apply. The fence shall be of wood, masonry or metal
and extend along the entire property line common to single-family use or zoning.

Section 4.17 Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU)

a. Applicability. The provisions of this section shall apply in all zoning
districts to all accessory dwelling units, as defined below. Any
property within the City containing a single-family residence may
apply for a permit to construct one (1) accessory dwelling unit, in
conformance with this section.

b. Purpose. Pursuant to Act 313 as provided by the 95" General
Assembly of the State of Arkansas, the following regulations are
adopted. Further, the city recognizes the following additional
purposes of this section:

i. To regulate Accessory Dwelling Units (ADU’s) to the extent
allowed by the State of Arkansas, to best retain the existing
character of Cabot;

ii. To expand housing options throughout the City of Cabot in a
manner that is compatible with the community; and

iii. To provide better flexibility for residents who wish to age in
place and continue living on their property.

c. Definitions.

i, Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU.) A self-contained and independently
accessed living unit on the same parcel as a single-family dwelling
of greater square footage that includes its own cooking, sleeping,
and sanitation facilities and complies with or is otherwise exempt
from any applicable regulatory requirements. For the purpose of
these regulations, an ADU may be attached, detached, or internal to
the primary house.

ii. Gross floor area. The interior habitable area of a single-family
dwelling or an accessory dwelling unit.

d. “By-Right” Use. Per Act 313, accessory dwelling units are allowed “By
Right” and applications meeting the provisions of this section may not
otherwise be required to obtain or be subject to:

i. A public hearing;
ii. A variance, conditional use permit, special permit, special exception;
or i
iii. Any other discretionary zoning action beyond a determination that the
plot plan does or does not conform to the applicable provisions of
this section.

e. Zoning Standards.

i. Zoning District Regulations. Accessory dwelling units (ADU’s) shall
comply with all underlying zoning requirements as prescribed for
single-family dwellings in the subject zoning district. Such zoning
requirements include the following:

a. Maximum Occupancy. Occupancy of the ADU shall be limited
to one (1) family.
b. Number Allowed. One (1) ADU per lot or parcel with an

c. Height Limitations. ADU’s shall not exceed the height
limitations provided in the applicable zoning district.

d. Lot Coverage. The total coverage for all buildings, including
the ADU, shall not exceed the maximum lot coverage amount
provided in the applicable zoning district.

e. Setbacks. ADU’s shall be subject to the same setbacks as
required by the zoning district for Single-Family dwellings, as
provided in Section 4.2, Residential District Regulations,
unless otherwise denoted within the subject zoning district. In
instances where the existing primary residence is built at a
distance greater than the minimum front setback, the front edge
of the principal building shall be established as the front
setback.

f. Lot Size. The Jot where the existing primary residence is
located and the ADU is proposed, must meet the current
minimum lot size requirements for the subject zoning district
for Single-Family dwellings, as provided in Section 4.2,
Residential District Regulations. However, ADU’s are not
subject to requirements for density limits, lot frontage, and
minimum land area per dwelling unit within the subject zoning
district.

g. ADU Size. Subject to all other requirements in this section, the
gross square footage of an ADU (both attached or detached
ADU) shall be no greater than seventy-five percent (75%) of
the square footage of the primary dwelling, or one-thousand
square feet (1,000 sq. fi.), whichever is less. If detached, the
ADU must also be a minimum of four hundred (400) square
feet in gross floor area.

following standards for administrative review by the building inspector, or
other appropriate city official. Prior to approval of the permit, the building
inspector or other appropriate city official shall verify compliance with the
following procedures:

application, including all requested plans, documents, details, and
fees.

ii. Exhibit/Plan. Applicant shall provide a scaled plan or exhibit
indicating all existing and proposed improvements on the property,
in accordance with these regulations and the adopted building
permit provisions.

iii, Fees.

a. Application Review Fee. A non-refundable review fee of two
hundred fifty dollars ($250).

b. Building Permit Fee. A non-refundable building permit fee
shall be required as indicated in the building permit fee
schedule.

c. Impact Fees. Applicable impact fees may be assessed for the
construction of an ADU up to a maximum of two hundred fifty

dollars ($250) per ADU.

iv. Zoning Standards. All applications shall provide the necessary data
and information on the plot plan to depict and achieve conformance
with the zoning standards provided in the above subsection.

v. Arkansas Fire Prevention Code. All applications shall provide the
necessary data and information to depict and achieve conformance
with the Arkansas Fire Prevention Code.

vi. Water and Sewer. Applications will not be approved until the applicant
has provided the city with a “will-serve” memo from the applicable
water and sewer provider or ADH approval for water/wastewater

Provisions not regulated or required. Per Act 313, accessory dwelling units

i. Requirement that the ADU match the exterior design, roof pitch, or
finishing materials of the single-family dwelling;
ili, Require that the single-family dwelling or the accessory dwelling unit
be occupied by the owner;
iv. Require a familial, marital, or employment relationship between the
occupants of the single-family dwelling and the occupants of the
ADU;
vy. Require improvements to public streets or sidewalks as a condition of
permitting the ADU, except as necessary to reconstruct or repair a
public street or sidewalk that is disturbed as a result of the
construction of the ADU;
vi. Require a restrictive covenant as a part of the ADU approval;
vii. Require separate water and sewer meter/service from the primary
structure.

Repair of Public Infrastructure. Any public infrastructure onsite or adjacent
to the project site that is disturbed or damaged as a result of the
construction of the ADU shall be repaired or replaced-as determined by the
city-prior to the Certificate of Occupancy issuance. The Applicant is
responsible for any such repair and/or replacing of disturbed or damaged
public infrastructure and any such work shall be done at the Applicant’s
expense. Images of existing infrastructure, including but not limited to
streets, curbs, street trees, drainage features, and other utilities shall be filed
with the application prior to issuance of the building permit.

Existing Detached Secondary (Accessory) Dwellings. Existing accessory
dwelling units permitted or constructed prior to the adoption of these
regulations shall be considered a legal and conforming accessory dwelling
on the property.

4.8.3 Procedure and Authority – Current Code

The procedure for the zoning of property to one of the above three classifications shall be the
same as for any other zoning application. The Planning Commission may outline special
parameters or special concerns which will apply to the Site Plan when such are identified through
the zoning process.

The Site Plan Review process occurs when a building permit is requested. The Building
Inspector and the Planning Commission shall review Site Plans prior to the issuance of a building
permit. At that time, the plan will be assessed for compatibility with standards and criteria
provided herein. Review of a Site Plan proposal shall take place at regularly scheduled monthly
meetings at which time interested persons may appear and offer information in support of or
against the proposed Site Plan. The Administrative Official will make recommendations to the
full Planning Commission at said public meeting and said Commission will then take one of the
following steps: approve the Site Plan as submitted; approve the Site Plan with modifications;
defer the Site Plan for future review; or deny the Site Plan.

In addition to the special requirements of this section, the Planning Commission may impose on
a Site Plan such additional requirements as are necessary to safeguard the public health, safety
and general welfare. The Planning Commission may require the Applicant to submit a revised
Site Plan incorporating the imposed requirements and modifications. Such revised Site Plans
shall have priority over new applications in the review process. The Planning commission may
deny a Site Plan and recommend reducing the zoning classification of any parcel which requires
a Site Plan if it does not carry out the general purpose of this section. In those instances where a
variance from district standards is requested as a part of the submittal request, the Planning
Commission may modify or waive standards. A variance may be allowed only after
demonstration of a hardship unique to the development proposal filed. Pecuniary difficulties
shall not be deemed to constitute a hardship.

Site plans will be reviewed by the Planning Commission under the following circumstances. All
other Site Plans shall be considered minor Site Plans and shall be reviewed by the staff.

 a. Buildings or developments placed on a plot of real property of two acres or larger.
 b. Any development containing a building with a combined square footage of 5,000 square
 feet or more.
 c. All multi-family housing developments containing twenty or more units.
 d. Any building or development storing, using or selling petroleum products, flammable
 products or hazardous materials.
 e. Any project referred by the City Staff.

5.4.6 Platted Building Lines and Buffers – Current Code

 a. Building lines for residential lots shall be at least twenty-five (25) feet from each street
 property line except in the following circumstances:

 i. Residential lots fronting on a minor arterial street shall have a platted building line
 not less than thirty-five (35) feet from the right-of-way line;
 ii. Residential lots fronting on principal arterials shall have a platted building line not
 less than forty (40) feet from the right-of-way line.

 b. Along arterial streets where it is desirable to limit curb access, building lines shall be
 established on both frontages of double frontage lots. Along the line of lots abutting such
 traffic artery, a restricted access easement of at least ten (10) feet, across which there
 shall be no right-of-vehicle access permitted, shall be provided.
 c. Multi-family (more than two units attached) subdivisions abutting single-family
 subdivisions or areas zoned for single-family use shall protect such areas from potential
 nuisance by providing a minimum forty (40)-foot buffer strip and a six (6)-foot fence of
 wood or masonry, extending along the entire abutting portion of the property. In those
 instances where drives or parking areas are proposed for intrusion into the buffer strip, a
 minimum of fifteen (15) feet shall be retained in its natural state. If ground cover and
 trees are sparse or have been removed, the fifteen (15)-foot strip shall be replanted with
 cover of the type natural to the area. No building, outside storage areas or sanitation
 equipment shall be permitted within the fifteen (15)-foot area.
 d. In those instances where a twenty-five (25)-foot permanent landscaped rear yard is
 provided, the buffer may be reduced to twenty-five (25) feet. In this arrangement, no
 structural or physical improvements are allowed within the twenty-five (25)-foot buffer.

 and extend along the entire property line common to single-family use or zoning.

Proposed Code:
Section 4.17 Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU)
 a. Applicability. The provisions of this section shall apply in all zoning districts to all
 accessory dwelling units, as defined below. Any property within the City containing
 a single-family residence may apply for a permit to construct one (1) accessory
 dwelling unit, in conformance with this section.

 b. Purpose. Pursuant to Act 313 as provided by the 95th General Assembly of the State
 of Arkansas, the following regulations are adopted. Further, the city recognizes the
 following additional purposes of this section:
 i. To regulate Accessory Dwelling Units (ADU’s) to the extend allowed by the
 State of Arkansas, to best retain the existing character of Cabot;
 ii. To expand housing options throughout the City of Cabot in a manner that is
 compatible with the community; and
 iii. To provide better flexibility for residents who wish to age in place and
 continue living on their property.

 c. Definitions.
 i. Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU.) A self-contained and independently
 accessed living unit on the same parcel as a single-family dwelling of greater
 square footage that includes its own cooking, sleeping, and sanitation
 facilities and complies with or is otherwise exempt from any applicable
 regulatory requirements. For the purpose of these regulations, an ADU may
 be attached, detached, or internal to the primary house.
 ii. Gross floor area. The interior habitable area of a single-family dwelling or
 an accessory dwelling unit.

 d. “By-Right” Use. Per Act 313, as provided by the 95th General Assembly of the State
 of Arkansas, accessory dwelling units are allowed “By Right” and applications
 meeting the provisions of this section may not otherwise be required to obtain or be
 subject to:
 i. A public hearing;
 ii. A variance, conditional use permit, special permit, special exception; or
 iii. Any other discretionary zoning action beyond a determination that the plot
 plan does or does not conform to the applicable provisions of this section.

 e. Zoning Standards.
 i. Zoning District Regulations. Accessory dwelling units (ADU’s) shall
 comply with all underlying zoning requirements as prescribed for single-
 family dwellings in the subject zoning district. Such zoning requirements
 include the following:
 a. Maximum Occupancy. Occupancy of the ADU shall be limited to one
 (1) family.
 b. Number Allowed. One (1) ADU per lot or parcel with an existing single-
 family primary dwelling shall be allowed.
 c. Height Limitations. ADU’s shall not exceed the height limitations
 provided in the applicable zoning district.
 d. Lot Coverage. The total coverage for all buildings, including the ADU,
 shall not exceed the maximum lot coverage amount provided in the
 applicable zoning district.

 e. Setbacks. ADU’s shall be subject to the same setbacks as required by the
 zoning district for Single-Family dwellings, as provided in Section 4.2,
 Residential District Regulations, unless otherwise denoted within the
 subject zoning district. In instances where the existing primary residence
 is built at a distance greater than the minimum front setback, the front
 edge of the principal building shall be established as the front setback.
 f. Lot Size. The lot where the existing primary residence is located and the
 ADU is proposed, must meet the current minimum lot size requirements
 for the subject zoning district for Single-Family dwellings, as provided
 in Section 4.2, Residential District Regulations. However, ADU’s are
 not subject to requirements for density limits, lot frontage, and minimum
 land area per dwelling unit within the subject zoning district.
 g. ADU Size. Subject to all other requirements in this section, the gross
 square footage of an ADU (both attached or detached ADU) shall be no
 greater than seventy-five percent (75%) of the square footage of the
 primary dwelling, or one-thousand square feet (1,000 sq. ft.), whichever
 is less. If detached, the ADU must also be a minimum of four hundred
 (400) square feet in gross floor area.

f. Review Procedures. All proposed accessory dwelling units shall meet the following
 standards for administrative review by the building inspector, or their designee. Prior
 to approval of the permit, the building inspector shall verify compliance with the
 following procedures.

 i. Application. Applicant shall provide a complete building permit application,
 including all required plans, documents, details, and fees.
 ii. Exhibit/Plan. Applicant shall provide a scaled plan or exhibit indicating all
 existing and proposed improvements on the property, in accordance with
 these regulations and the adopted building permit provisions.
 iii. Fees.
 a. Application Review Fee. A non-refundable review fee of two hundred
 fifty dollars ($250).
 b. Building Permit Fee. A non-refundable building permit fee shall be
 required as indicated in the building permit fee schedule.
 c. Impact Fees. Applicable adopted impact fees may be assessed for the
 construction of an ADU up to a maximum of two hundred fifty dollars
 ($250) per ADU.
 iv. Zoning Standards. All applications shall provide the necessary data and
 information on the plot plan to depict and achieve conformance with the
 zoning standards provided in the above subsection.
 v. Arkansas Fire Prevention Code. All applications shall provide the necessary
 data and information to depict and achieve conformance with the Arkansas
 Fire Prevention Code.
 vi. Water and Sewer. Applications will not be approved until the applicant has
 provided the city with a “well-serve” memo from the applicable water and
 sewer provider or ADH approval for water/wastewater supply where public
 water or sewer is not available.

g. Provisions not regulated or required. Per Act 313, accessory dwelling units are
 allowed “By Right” and the following may not be required or regulated with the
 permitting of an ADU:

 i. Additional parking to accommodate the ADU or fees in lieu of additional
 parking;
 ii. Requirement that the ADU match the exterior design, roof pitch, or finishing
 materials of the single-family dwelling;
 iii. Require that the single-family dwelling or the accessory dwelling unit be
 occupied by the owner;
 iv. Require a familial, marital, or employment relationship between the
 occupants of the single-family dwelling and the occupants of the ADU;
 v. Require improvements to public streets or sidewalks as a condition of
 permitting the ADU, except as necessary to reconstruct or repair a public
 street or sidewalk that is disturbed as a result of the construction of the ADU;
 vi. Require a restrictive covenant as a part of the ADU approval;
 vii. Require separate water and sewer meter/service from the primary structure.

h. Repair of Public Infrastructure. Any public infrastructure onsite or adjacent to the
 project site that is disturbed or damaged as a result of the construction of the ADU
 shall be repaired or replaced-as determined by the city-prior to the Certificate of
 Occupancy issuance. Images of existing infrastructure, including but not limited to
 streets, curbs, street trees, drainage features, and other utilities shall be filed with the
 application prior to issuance of the building permit.

i. Existing Detached Secondary (Accessory) Dwellings. Existing accessory dwelling
 units permitted or constructed prior to the adoption of these regulations shall be
 considered a legal and conforming accessory dwelling on the property.

Webber, Corey Spangler, and Brandon Hillenburg. Others present were
Mayor Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper, Deputy City Attorney Courtnie
Holt, and City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

by title. The motion passed unanimously.

A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING AND DIRECTING THE RETURN
OF FUNDS TO THE CABOT WATER AND WASTEWATER
COMMISSION UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS; AMENDING THE
GENERAL FUND OF THE 2025 ANNUAL OPERATING BUDGET;
AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, in Resolution 8 of 2024, the Cabot City Council authorized the City to
accept the donation of certain specified real property for use as a public park; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council further authorized the City to enter into an agreement
with the Cabot Water and Waste Water Commission to provide sewer infrastructure and related
services for the proposed park. Pursuant to that agreement the Commission would also contribute

funds towards the infrastructure’s installation. The sewer infrastructure was subsequently installed and
the Commission contributed $50,705.40 to the total cost of the project; and

WHEREAS, as of the passage of this resolution, the real property in question has not been
donated to the City and, as such, has not been dedicated as a public park. The Cabot City Council
therefore determines that the infrastructure installation is not at this time in furtherance of a public
park and that the funds contributed to the project by the Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission
to that end should be refunded to it.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: Contingent upon the conditions set forth later in this Section, the
Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized and directed to return the funds paid
by the Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission pursuant to the agreement authorized by
Resolution 8 of 2024. The total amount authorized and directed to be paid to the Cabot
Water and Wastewater Commission is $50,705.40. The authorizations and directions
provided for herein shall not take effect if the real property referred to herein and in
Resolution 8 of 2024 has been acquired and by the City and dedicated as a public park by

August 30, 2025.

SECTION 2: The General Fund of the 2025 Annual Operating Budget is hereby

amended to accommodate the $50,705.40 payment authorized and directed herein.
